question: What is your exact beef mince formula?
answer: Strictly 80% lean beef and 20% natural fat, passed through the mincer twice. The fat keeps the burger juicy and caramelized; double mincing gives a fine, cohesive binder so the patty never breaks on the griddle, with no egg or breadcrumbs needed. Keep mince chilled at 2-4°C.

question: Do you press the patty after flipping?
answer:
• Heat a heavy flat cast-iron griddle to 220-240°C until light wisps of smoke appear.
• Place the cold 85-90 g ball on the dry, un-oiled griddle.
• Cover with a small square of parchment/butter paper.
• Press with the heavy smash tool using full body weight for 10 seconds until paper-thin with ragged, lacy edges.
• Remove the paper; season immediately with fine salt and cracked black pepper.
• Sear side 1 undisturbed for 60-90 seconds until edges are dark brown and crispy.
• Slide a stiff, sharp metal scraper fully under the crust and flip in one clean motion.
• Immediately lay a cheddar slice on the hot patty.
• Cook side 2 for only 30-45 seconds until the cheese melts.
• Remove immediately. Never press the patty after flipping.

question: How do you make homemade pickles?
answer: We take cucumber and slice it properly. Then in around one cup of hot water we add approximately 3–4 tablespoons of vinegar, one small lemon, 2 tablespoons of sugar, and half a teaspoon of salt. We put the sliced cucumbers into this mixture and leave them for around 30 minutes. After that we let the pickles cool down in the same liquid. Once cooled, we store them in the refrigerator. Keeping them refrigerated helps preserve them properly.

question: Why does the patty break while frying?
answer: Sometimes our patty breaks while frying. One reason is accidentally adding too much butter to the patty mixture. Another is when we need to prepare the meat quickly and use a small amount of raw papaya paste to tenderize — if too much raw papaya paste is added, the mixture can release water, and that excess moisture makes the patty weak so it breaks while frying. We experienced this exact problem at our Habitt stall.

question: How do you build the Signature Alfredo white sauce?
answer: Melt 1 tablespoon pure butter over medium heat. Saute finely minced garlic for 30 seconds. Pour in chilled dairy cream and whole milk, stirring gently, and bring to a gentle simmer. Add our in-house secret spice blend (proprietary, never disclosed), plus black pepper and salt. Fold in grated cheddar and mozzarella with 2-3 tablespoons of reserved pasta water. Whisk until smooth, velvety and clinging to the back of a spoon. Toss in the penne and chicken for 60 seconds.

question: The burger patty turned out dry — what went wrong?
answer: Causes: (1) mince under 20% fat; (2) griddle too cold (below 200°C) so juices stew out instead of searing; (3) patty pressed after flipping. Fix: verify 80/20, heat the griddle to 220°C+ before the meat goes on, and smash once for 10 seconds, never again.

question: The Alfredo sauce is thin and watery — how do you fix it?
answer: Simmer on medium-low for an extra 90 seconds and add 2 tablespoons more grated cheese. If still thin, dissolve 1/2 teaspoon cornflour in 1 tablespoon cold milk, stir into the bubbling sauce and whisk 60 seconds until thick and glossy.

question: The Alfredo sauce split — how do you recover it?
answer: The pan got too hot and the dairy fat separated. Remove from the flame immediately and whisk in 2 tablespoons of warm starchy pasta water or cold milk vigorously; the sauce re-emulsifies within about 30 seconds.

question: Caramelized onions smell bitter — can they be salvaged?
answer: Cannot be salvaged. Burnt butter and scorched onion sugars taint the whole batch. Discard it, wash the pan, melt fresh butter over low flame and cook a new batch slowly. Never raise the heat to save time.
